issues.parameter: WD mass, mass ratio and inclination
issues.competing_evidence: Thomas+00 cyclotron/RV branch gives Mwd≈0.39 Msun, i≈66 deg and q=M2/Mwd≈1.1 for M2≈0.45; its stability-motivated branch is Mwd≈0.64 Msun, i≈45.3 deg but conflicts with the observed cyclotron spectrum. Gänsicke+00 obtains ≈0.40 Msun from the IUE radius at assumed 200 pc. Beuermann+20 rescales that same angular radius to Gaia d≈172 pc and obtains Rwd≈9.5e8 cm and implied Mwd≈0.57 Msun at fixed 15,000 K. Thomas+00 also discusses an evolved-donor branch Mwd≈0.31, M2≈0.25, still outside its stability criterion. No branch is an independent dynamical WD mass.
issues.why_it_matters: The WD mass and q determine whether the binary solution is dynamically stable and materially change comparisons of long-period polar masses with other radio-emitting WD populations. Choosing or averaging branches without a direct constraint would imply unsupported evolutionary conclusions.
issues.needed_action: Retain all branches as model-dependent. For a preferred value, obtain phase-resolved donor/RV constraints and a joint cyclotron/FUV solution with Gaia distance, and verify whether the donor is evolved or out of thermal equilibrium. No scalar WD mass is currently selected.

issues.competing_evidence: Barrett+20 Table 2 gives B=3563±730 G only under the assumption of fundamental electron-cyclotron-maser emission from the donor corona; the source is not spatially resolved to a component, and Table 1/text report strong polarization in the first detection but no polarization in the second without mapping the epochs/states. Thomas+00 independently finds 56 MG optical cyclotron field in a WD accretion region. These fields describe different emitting regions and mechanisms.
issues.why_it_matters: Mistaking the conditional kG radio-emission field for a WD field would erase the distinction between radio and optical diagnostics and distort the field distribution of the catalog.
issues.needed_action: Keep the 3.56-kG value conditional and separate. Confirm with epoch-resolved radio spectra/polarization and an optical accretion-state record; localize the source if possible before assigning the emitting region or mechanism.

issues.parameter: X-ray flux band and absorption convention
issues.competing_evidence: The exact 4XMM-DR11 source is 0.591 arcsec from Gaia and has one detection with mean catalog 0.2–12 keV flux 9.96521±0.382865e-13 erg cm-2 s-1. Ridder+23 Table 3 approximates 1–10 keV as the full band minus 0.2–0.5 and 0.5–1 keV, and 0.1–10 as the full band assuming negligible 10–12 keV photons; it imposes a ≥10% error floor. issues.parameter: WD spin versus orbital period / small asynchronism
issues.competing_evidence: Thomas+00 and van der Heyden+02 phase the polarimetric emission on the 4.19021016-h orbital ephemeris and use the conventional synchronized-polar interpretation. Gänsicke+00 explicitly notes that more accurate ephemerides are needed to test for a small residual asynchronism. No independent spin period or beat period was found in the searched source literature.
issues.why_it_matters: A confirmed asynchronous spin would change the physical subtype and the clock interpretation used in comparisons among magnetic CVs.
issues.needed_action: Keep the numerical WD-spin field blank and synchronization labeled as the polar interpretation. Resolve only with modern high-speed timing/polarimetry spanning enough cycles to separate Porb and Pspin.
